 It’s time for your weekly roundup of the latest  OTT and theatrical releases! The next seven days bring a diverse mix of films and shows across genres, offering plenty of options for your weekend watchlist. 
 From gripping crime dramas and romantic stories to big-screen spectacles and festive entertainers, here’s everything arriving this week.

 OTT Releases This Week
 The Greatest (November 4)
 Streaming on Prime Video 
 © Amazon Prime Video 
 This biographical series explores the life and legacy of boxing icon  Muhammad Ali . It follows his journey to the top of the heavyweight division while also examining his political activism, religious conversion and eventual exile from boxing. The narrative places his sporting achievements against the backdrop of the social and political changes that shaped the 1960s and 1970s. 
 Dilwali Diwali (November 5)
 Streaming on Netflix 
 © Netflix 
 Directed by Ritesh Menon, this family drama follows a young man, played by Mihir Ahuja, who returns home for Diwali, setting off a series of emotional revelations and clashes between generations. Produced by Terribly Tiny Tales, the film also stars Manoj Pahwa and Neelu Kohli, who navigate the complicated relationships within an extended family. 
 Black Doves Season 2 (November 5)
 Streaming on Netflix 
 © Netflix 
 Keira Knightley and Ben Whishaw return for the second season of this British spy thriller. The new instalment follows Helen Webb as she struggles to keep her secret life as an assassin hidden from her husband, whose political ambitions are now taking him closer to becoming Prime Minister. As her personal and professional worlds collide, maintaining control over her covert network becomes increasingly difficult. 
 North of North Season 2 (November 5)
 Streaming on Netflix 
 © Netflix 
 The Canadian comedy returns to the Arctic community of Ice Cove, where winter brings fresh challenges for its residents. The new season follows Siaja, an ambitious young Inuk mother, as she tries to prove to her boss that she is capable of taking on responsibilities beyond managing a calendar. Alongside its small-town humour, the series explores her changing priorities and personal struggles. 
 One Year to Live, Buy a Man (November 5)
 Streaming on Netflix 
 © Netflix 
 Based on a popular webcomic, this Japanese romantic drama follows a young woman who receives a terminal diagnosis and learns that she has only a year to live. Deciding to make the most of her remaining time, she offers financial support to a struggling aspiring actor in exchange for his company. However, what begins as a transactional arrangement gradually develops into a genuine emotional bond. 
 Haiwaan (November 6)
 Streaming on SonyLIV 
 © KVN Productions 
 Directed by Priyadarshan, this thriller is an official remake of the 2016 Malayalam film Oppam . Saif Ali Khan plays a blind caretaker who discovers a dead body and finds himself under suspicion for the murder. With the police closing in, he must rely on his heightened senses to uncover the truth and identify the real killer, played by Akshay Kumar. 
 Meesaya Murukku 2 (November 6)
 Streaming on SonyLIV 
 © Avni Movies 
 Hiphop Tamizha Adhi returns with the sequel to his 2017 Tamil musical comedy, which arrives on OTT just in time for Diwali. The story follows Jeeva, an aspiring musician whose relationship with Laila is put to the test when the son of a powerful film producer develops an interest in her. As the conflict unfolds, Jeeva also discovers a forgotten chapter of his family's musical history. Adhi takes on multiple roles across different generations. 
 Theatrical Releases
 Ramayana (November 5)
 © Prime Focus Studios 
 Nitesh Tiwari's ambitious adaptation of the Indian epic arrives in cinemas as the first instalment of a two-part saga.  Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi portrays Sita, while Yash takes on the role of Ravana. The ensemble also features Sunny Deol as Hanuman, with the story bringing the timeless mythology to the big screen on a grand scale. 
 Scene (November 6)
 © Zhagaran Studios 
 Suriya teams up with Aavesham and Romancham director Jithu Madhavan for this Tamil action comedy. The film also stars Nazriya Nazim and Naslen, bringing together a mix of familiar Malayalam cinema talent for the filmmaker's first Tamil directorial venture. The story centres on an unconventional police team whose latest assignment takes them into increasingly unpredictable situations. 
 Mookuthi Amman 2 (November 6)
 © Vels Film International 
 Nayanthara returns as the titular goddess in this fantasy-comedy sequel, directed by Sundar C. Unlike the first film, which was directed by RJ Balaji, the sequel expands the story with a new supernatural conflict. The cast also includes Regina Cassandra, Urvashi, Yogi Babu and Duniya Vijay, among others.
